svg.title: Trajectory Annotation — the complete method
svg.desc: Both stages of trajectory annotation on one canvas. Stage 1 interpolates context across scattered stations to the moving object's position, one epoch at a time. Stage 2 fits a curve through the resulting time series and reads it at that object's exact timestamp. The result is a contextually enriched trajectory.
svg.text: Linking every trajectory point to the conditions the moving object passed through — so movement can be read in context.
context is never measured where — or when — the object is
Not when the object is there
context is observed far less often than position
Spatial — across stations, one epoch at a time
Interpolated straight to the object's position in projected metres · no raster is built · a surface is available on request
Hold out a station, predict it from the rest, compare with what it observed · one method for all epochs by default, or chosen per epoch
A time series at the object's position
one value per epoch — exactly what stage 2 needs
Bearings interpolate on the unit circle — stations reading 350° and 10° must give 0°, not 180°. The caller declares which variables are circular.
Points outside the station hull are reported as missing, not invented.
Temporal — through time, at that position
A curve fitted through the epoch series, then read at the object's exact timestamp
Candidate methods · fitted to the series from stage 1
degrees 2–7 · least-squares, passes near the points
Eq. 3 · window = degree + 2, sharing a breakpoint
k = 2…10 · first and last observation always kept in training, so no method is asked to extrapolate · averaged over all k folds
fitted on every observation, ready to use
Selection runs once per context variable, per location — wind direction may be best served by a spline, wave height by another method entirely.
Bearings interpolate on the unit circle here too; the caller declares which variables are circular.
Every object crossing this area and period reads from the same fitted curve
Read the fitted curve at each timestamp
A trajectory that carries its context can be analysed for how the environment shaped the movement — and it is the input the rest of the method set needs.
Feature selection — which context factors actually matter
CADP — compression that keeps context-bearing points
Stage 2 is the method of Mehri, Alesheikh & Basiri (2023) §4.1. Stage 1 extends it — the paper generated per-epoch surfaces but placed the study of spatial interpolation outside its scope.
